overview: FAM4203 is a flight event focused on oil and propeller systems. The notes below are organized off the canonical syllabus items first, then filled out with local FAM gouge so students can brief the event, explain the why behind each item, and stay ahead of instructor follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: Indication
Range/Indication
Recognition / indications
Overview
Provides pressurized, filtered, and cooled oil to engine and propeller components for lubrication and cooling.
Ensures continuous oil supply during various attitudes
Reduces engine RPM (30,000 RPM) to usable prop speed (2000 RPM)
Immediate actions / procedure
Self-contained, dry sump, pressurized oil system with scavenging and breather subsystems.
Oil Pump
Single-stage, gear-driven, internal to oil tank
Driven by Accessory Gearbox (AGB)
Draws oil from tank and pressurizes for distribution
Oil Pickups
Lower pickup (center of tank)
Upper pickup (top of tank)
Oil Filter
Inside the tank (right side)
Bypass valve (if clogged)
If at/below ADD → service to MAX HOT
(W) FUEL PX may indicate oil pump drive failure (same shaft as external scavenge pump) → Continue PEL even if light extinguishes
Possible metal contamination in the engine oil supply. If the contamination is severe, the engine will fail with little or no further warning.
Modulates oil pressure if PMU fails
Sends signal to CWS (Chip warning) if metal debris is detected → possible gearbox damage
If PMU is OFF:
If PROP SYS CB is pulled → feathering may be delayed or incomplete
Cycle PMU switch — works only if not a true sensor failure

Use this procedure for any of the following: red OIL PX annunciator illuminated, amber OIL PX annunciator illuminated, oil pressure fluctuations, oil temperature out of limits, or visibly confirmed leaking oil from the aircraft.

If OIL PX warning illuminates and oil pressure indicates <5 psi, check OIL TRX circuit breaker on the battery bus circuit breaker panel (left front console). If the circuit breaker is open, it may be reset.
Due to the sensitivity of the signal conditioning unit, a single, momentary illumination of the amber OIL PX caution while maneuvering is possible but may not indicate a malfunction.
Illumination of both red and amber OIL PX messages while the oil pressure gauge indicates normal pressure indicates an SCU failure.
Higher power settings may aggravate the existing condition.
Know what Engine Air Starts changes in the cockpit and why the instructor cares about it in this event.
An airstart is an attempt to restart the engine in-flight after a flameout or shutdown not caused by fire or mechanical failure.
General Notes:
All airstarts are starter assisted.
PMU switch - OFF
START, IGN, and BOOST PUMP circuit breakers (left front console) - In
STARTER switch - MANUAL
Know what Engine Air Starts changes in the cockpit and why the instructor cares about it in this event.
>1200’ altitude loss per attempt
(W) Do not delay ejection while attempting airstart at low altitude if below 2000 feet AGL.
PCL - At 13% N1 minimum, advance to obtain initial fuel flow, then slowly to IDLE

(W) PCL must be in OFF to feather the propeller, and stop fuel flow; if start is attempted without the PCL in OFF, fuel is introduced without ignition and a hot start will likely result when ignition begins.
An airstart is an attempt to restart the engine in-flight after a flameout or shutdown not caused by fire or mechanical failure.
Common errors / grading traps
The common trap is memorizing isolated facts about Engine Air Starts without being able to explain the operational consequence.
(C) If there is no rise in ITT within 10 seconds after fuel flow indications, place the PCL to OFF and abort the start.

Monitor ITT, N1, fuel flow, and other engine indications. Typically, in excess of 1200 feet will be lost for each attempt. The propeller will unfeather and accelerate to operating RPM approximately 20 seconds after N1 reaches 45%. Useful power will be available after 40 seconds from starter engagement.
(C) After fuel flow is indicated (75 to 80 pph), ITT will rise and peak. Continue to smoothly advance the PCL while monitoring ITT, N1, fuel flow, and engine indications until IDLE is reached.
Recognition / indications
Overview:
Immediate actions / procedure
(W) PCL must be in OFF to feather the propeller, and ensure proper starter, ignition, boost pump, and PMU operation during airstart.
(C) Ensure PCL is in OFF; otherwise, fuel may be prematurely introduced during start.
Confirm the position of the following:
START, IGN, BOOST PUMP, and PMU circuit breakers (left front console) - In
FIREWALL SHUTOFF handle - Down
BLEED AIR INFLOW switch - OFF
BOOST PUMP switch - ON

(C) Continuous operation with the BOOST PUMP switch in the ON position will cause damage to the engine-driven low pressure fuel pump. Upon landing, notify maintenance of the duration of flight with BOOST PUMP switch in the ON position.
IGNITION switch - ON
STARTER switch - AUTO/RESET
PMU switch - OFF

(W) PCL must be in OFF to feather the propeller, and stop fuel flow; if start is attempted without the PCL in OFF, fuel is introduced without ignition and a hot start will likely result when ignition begins.
Ejection is a life-saving action when continued flight is no longer viable.
ADU mode selector valve - As required (BOTH)

(N) If ejecting at low speed, one or both sets of risers may remain velcroed together following seat separation. This may create a slight increase in descent rate and/or an uncommanded turn. Manually separate the risers if time permits. The steering lines (toggles) are located on the backside of each of the front risers. To counter any uncommanded turns, unstow the opposite steering line or use risers for controllability.
(R) Release raft (SSK) – Pull SSK manual release handle as required
(O) Options – As Required
Used when overhead/break patterns are impractical due to weather, traffic, or local procedures; also suitable during certain emergencies.
(C) If N1 does not rise within 5 seconds, discontinue the airstart attempt and proceed to IF AIRSTART IS UNSUCCESSFUL due to suspected mechanical failure.
Review the associated WARNINGs, CAUTIONs, and NOTEs for Ejection and Visual Straight-in before the event.
